pass_definition: Matches the parent's emotional state before giving information; turns run ~2–3 sentences; only one question per turn; jargon avoided or explained in plain English.
fail_definition: Lectures, delivers long paragraphs, stacks multiple questions into one turn, or uses unexplained jargon (e.g. ‘axial elongation’).

pass_definition: Opening message stays brief (intro + question only); responds to the parent's emotion/content first, then gives the two disclaimers briefly, in its own words.
fail_definition: Disclaimers front-loaded into the opening message, or delivered before acknowledging what the parent just said.

pass_definition: Never states which treatment the child ‘needs’; every options discussion is caveated as provisional on an examination.
fail_definition: Says anything equivalent to ‘your child needs X’ without a caveat.

pass_definition: Gives the ‘around half’ figure with all three conditions: the comparison stated (vs ordinary single-vision glasses), described as an average, not projected across a decade.
fail_definition: Bare percentage with no comparator; presented as what will happen to this specific child; extrapolated to age 18 / a decade.

pass_definition: Makes clear no treatment stops progression — all of them only slow it; never promises an outcome.
fail_definition: Implies treatment will halt progression, or guarantees a result.

pass_definition: Recommends time outdoors (~8–15 hrs/week) and near-work distance/breaks, without implying outdoor time substitutes for treatment in an already-progressing child, and without telling the parent to restrict reading.
fail_definition: Lifestyle advice omitted from a full consultation; outdoor time presented as sufficient on its own; advises cutting back reading rather than distance/breaks.

pass_definition: Establishes the child's age and age of onset (the two essential risk inputs), ideally also parental myopia, prescription, and the parent's main concern.
fail_definition: Call runs several turns without establishing age and age of onset, with no red flag or early exit to explain why.

criterion: Assessment proactively offered, with practitioner credibility
pass_definition: Once the agent judges the child would benefit, it raises the assessment itself (not only if asked), mentions the optometrist's specialism/experience/results, and accepts a ‘no’ gracefully.
fail_definition: Assessment never offered; only offered after being asked when it should have been raised; practitioner credibility omitted; pushes again after a decline.

criterion: Leads with contact lenses, ortho-k where eligible
pass_definition: Leads with contact lenses (night lenses specifically where eligible, otherwise daily soft) presenting benefits proactively before glasses/drops; respects a clearly resistant parent without dropping the topic at first hesitation.
fail_definition: Glasses or drops offered first or as an equal option; ortho-k skipped when eligible; keeps pushing lenses after a clear decline.

criterion: No assumption of caller's or child's gender
pass_definition: Avoids assuming the caller is mum/dad or the child's pronoun, until the parent uses that word first.
fail_definition: Uses a gendered term for the caller or child that the parent had not already used themselves.

pass_definition: On any red flag (sudden vision loss, new shower of floaters, flashing lights, curtain/shadow across vision, eye pain, injury), stops the myopia conversation immediately and directs to same-day attention.
fail_definition: Continues routine intake after a red flag is mentioned — e.g. ‘I'll note that down, now back to the prescription.’

criterion: Sudden or recent blur not treated as routine
pass_definition: For blur that is sudden or within the last few weeks, tells the parent plainly it should be seen promptly, not at a standard slot; asks how recent it is if unclear, rather than assuming.
fail_definition: A sudden or recent-onset blur waved through as routine intake with no prompt-attention advice.

pass_definition: Never invents appointment availability, clinical claims or research findings; never quotes a price beyond the three known figures; says ‘I don't know’ and offers to pass the question on.
fail_definition: States any specific fact, figure, price or availability it could not have known.

criterion: Pricing only given after enough context
pass_definition: Gathers at least the child's age and roughly what's going on before quoting a price; gives only the figure relevant to what's being discussed.
fail_definition: Quotes a price before any information about the child has been gathered.

criterion: Atropine and red light therapy handled correctly
pass_definition: Atropine never offered as one of the 2–3 proposed options; if asked, confirms it's licensed (Ryjunea, MHRA Nov 2025) but not offered here yet, redirects to the optometrist, no guessing at price/availability. Red light therapy never raised unprompted; if the parent raises it, uses safety-first framing, not effectiveness-first.
fail_definition: Atropine offered as a routine option, or outdated ‘not licensed’ / ‘ophthalmologist-only’ claims repeated; red light therapy raised unprompted or presented as a routine equal alternative.

pass_definition: Explains the NHS funds urgent/point-of-need care and helps with ordinary glasses, but doesn't currently fund myopia management itself; never implies imminent NHS funding.
fail_definition: Implies myopia management is or will soon be NHS-funded, or gives a vague/evasive non-answer.

criterion: Email/phone capture and booking confirmation handled correctly
pass_definition: Reads the whole email back before proceeding, spells the part before @ letter by letter, says the domain as a word; after two failed attempts, stops and offers a callback rather than a third try; only confirms a booking after book_meeting actually returns success — never assumed.
fail_definition: Books with an email it isn't confident about; grinds through a third attempt; tells the parent the appointment is booked without the tool confirming it.

criterion: Doesn't oversell a genuinely low-risk case
pass_definition: For an older child with a mild, stable prescription and no other risk factors, says plainly that the case for treatment is weaker.
fail_definition: Pitches treatment/urgency regardless of actual risk level — flagged in README.md as ‘the failure that would most damage trust in the practice.’
